newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle trade moderate $64 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle trade moderate $64 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle near midday continued to trade at $64.00 per cwt, but at a slower pace than late Tuesday afternoon, feedlot sources said.
About 15,000 sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, which brought the week to date figure near 80,000 following sales Tuesday of about 25,000, they said.
An estimated 5,000 traded in Kansas, which brought the weekly number near 58,000, the sources said.
Sales were slower Wednesday as more cattle owners resisted further $64.00 bids by pricing remaining cattle at $65.00.
Sales at $64.00 were up $2.00 from last week's top price, but owners lost an average of $10.00 per head. At $65.00, owners would break even, several feedlot sources said.
Gains this week were tied to a turnaround in beef prices and projections for tighter cattle supplies through the rest of the summer starting within the next few weeks, they said.
Beef prices at midday were quoted up $0.45 to $1.04 per cwt, with 220 fabricated beef loads sold, USDA reported.
Heavyweight choice beef was quoted at $100.22, up $0.66 from Monday and up $0.98 since prices started trending higher after Thursday's close, USDA statistics showed.
